issues.description:
Method return type mismatch for PersonService.savePerson(Person):
- In the template (src/server/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/service/PersonService.java) savePerson is declared to return Person (allows callers to obtain the created/updated entity).
- In the solution (src/server/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/service/PersonService.java) savePerson has been changed to return void.
- The solution's REST layer (src/server/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/rest/PersonResource.java) still calls personService.savePerson(...) inside ResponseEntity.ok(...) in both createPerson and updatePerson, i.e. it treats savePerson as if it returned a Person. This inconsistency will cause compilation errors and will confuse students about the intended service contract and how the controller obtains the saved/updated Person.
issues.suggestedFix:
Make the service contract and controller usage consistent. Two viable fixes:
1) Restore the service API to match the template: change PersonService.savePerson(Person) to return Person and return the created/updated Person. This keeps the controller code (ResponseEntity.ok(personService.savePerson(...))) unchanged and is the recommended fix to preserve the expected service semantics.
OR
2) Change the controller to match the void service: call personService.savePerson(person) (void), then explicitly return the Person instance (for example, ResponseEntity.ok(person)) or fetch the saved entity before returning. Ensure both createPerson and updatePerson consistently use the same approach.
